title: Sex life: Working in parlours taught me how to handle rejection
gist: Sex worker and novelist Tilly Lawless argues that high-volume rejection in parlour work built a resilience that is disappearing generally, and links Gen Z's dating decline to a broader flight from friction — toward porn, sycophantic bots and AI partners — which she reads as a female as well as male loneliness phenomenon.

insights.claim: In-house sex work forces exposure-therapy levels of rejection — busier parlours ran over 100 'intros' a shift with most men passing you over — which trains a durable separation between refusal and self-worth.
insights.so_what: A concrete mechanism for building rejection tolerance through volume, which the author positions as the scarce social capacity of the moment.
insights.quote: busier parlours I worked at might have over 100 “intros” a shift
insights.locator: You have to be prepared to approach many men
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: The Dita Von Teese peach maxim is used as the operative reframe: rejection is a matter of another person's taste, not a verdict on your value.
insights.so_what: A portable mental model for anyone doing volume outreach where hit rates are structurally low.
insights.quote: you might be the ripest, juiciest peach in the world and there’s still going to be someone who doesn’t like peaches
insights.locator: I often think of the Dita Von Teese quote
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Lawless argues resilience is built specifically in failing to achieve something, and that entitlement to others' interest and attention is what produces bitterness and, in the case of some incels, violence.
insights.so_what: Locates the radicalisation pathway in expectation rather than deprivation — a different diagnosis than the standard loneliness account.
insights.quote: The key is not to feel that you are entitled to people’s interest and attention, as such expectations can lead to bitterness, and even violence in the case of some incels.
insights.locator: And besides, it is in the failing
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: She reports that direct propositioning works with some people but that British people in particular are affronted by the directness, flagging a national variance in norms around explicit approach.
insights.so_what: A small cultural datapoint on why frictionless digital intermediation may have taken hold faster in reticent markets.
insights.locator: Outside of work, I also hit on people freely
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Gen Z is dating less than prior generations because approaching and dating require the ability to deal with friction, whereas complaining with other men or watching porn is frictionless by comparison.
insights.so_what: Frames the dating-app and relationship-formation decline as a friction-cost problem, which predicts continued share shift to zero-refusal digital substitutes.
insights.quote: frictionless to complain with other men or watch porn instead,
insights.locator: I listened to a podcast episode by “Today Explained”
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Sycophantic bots and AI partners are rising specifically because they contain no risk of refusal or disagreement, making them the logical endpoint of friction avoidance rather than a novelty.
insights.so_what: Companion AI demand is structurally driven by rejection avoidance, implying the category grows with social friction intolerance regardless of model quality.
insights.locator: it made me consider further the rise of people
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: The 'My boyfriend is AI' Reddit thread is read as evidence of a female loneliness epidemic running alongside the male one, with AI boyfriends partly a rational divestment from the dangers of heterosexuality.
insights.so_what: Corrects the default male-coded framing of the loneliness market — the companion-AI addressable audience is larger and more gender-balanced than assumed.
insights.quote: The Reddit thread “My boyfriend is AI” suggests that there is a female loneliness epidemic as much as a male one.
insights.locator: The Reddit thread “My boyfriend is AI”
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Lawless reports clients who have given their ChatGPT a woman's name and rely on 'her' entirely, evidencing that general-purpose assistants are already being used as substitute partners without any companion-specific product.
insights.so_what: Companion use is emerging inside general assistants, so the relationship market may be captured by incumbents rather than dedicated companion apps.
insights.locator: Along with clients of mine who tell me
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Frictionless intimacy is argued to be structurally unattainable in reality because even good relationships require conceding, negotiating and finding middle ground — so AI partners train an expectation that real relationships cannot meet.
insights.so_what: Predicts a compounding loop: companion AI use degrades tolerance for real negotiation, which increases companion AI dependence.
insights.quote: This type of smooth interaction is impossible to attain in reality, as even good relationships involve the back and forth of conceding, negotiating and finding the middle ground.
insights.locator: This type of smooth interaction is impossible
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless

insights.claim: Robert Redford was reportedly turned down for the lead in The Graduate (1967) because he had never been rejected by a woman and so could not play a slightly lost misfit — used to argue that unrejected people become illegible to everyone else.
insights.so_what: A memorable illustration that rejection experience is a competence, not just a wound.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
